editorial:
Imagine you are at a sunny backyard party with your family and friends. Everything is great until you realize your five-year-old son is gone. That is exactly how things start for Ryan, and it is a scary moment that any parent can relate to. But instead of just being relieved when the boy is found, Ryan snaps. He has a violent outburst that shocks everyone there. This one moment acts like a trigger, peeling back the layers of his life and showing you that he is carrying some heavy baggage from his own childhood. The movie feels like a slow burn that keeps you guessing about why Ryan is so broken inside.

The acting is the best part here because the emotions feel real and raw. You will find yourself rooting for Ryan even when he makes mistakes. While the middle part of the movie slows down a bit, the payoff is totally worth it. It is a perfect pick for a quiet night in when you want a story that actually makes you feel something.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Ryan finally confronts his father in a heated argument. He reveals that he spent his whole life trying not to be like him, but his outburst at the party proved he is still struggling. Ryan chooses to go to therapy and asks for forgiveness from his wife. The movie ends with a quiet moment between him and his son, showing that he is finally starting to heal and break the cycle of anger.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves character studies and stories about family healing.
